### Filtering highly variable features

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_var_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
In which .var slot to store a boolean array corresponding to the highly variable features.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"filter_with_hvg"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_obs_batch_key`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If specified, highly-variable features are selected within each batch separately and merged. This simple
process avoids the selection of batch-specific features and acts as a lightweight batch correction method.
For all flavors, featues are first sorted by how many batches they are highly variable. For dispersion-based flavors
ties are broken by normalized dispersion. If flavor = 'seurat_v3', ties are broken by the median (across
batches) rank based on within-batch normalized variance.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_flavor`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Choose the flavor for identifying highly variable features. For the dispersion based methods
in their default workflows, Seurat passes the cutoffs whereas Cell Ranger passes n_top_features.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"seurat"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"seurat"`, `"cell_ranger"`, `"seurat_v3"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_n_top_features`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of highly-variable features to keep. Mandatory if filter_with_hvg_flavor is set to 'seurat_v3'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_var_name_filter_to_exclude`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
List of feature names to exclude from HVG calculation.
Common use cases include excluding mitochondrial genes, ribosomal genes,
or cell cycle genes that may dominate variance but are not biologically
informative for clustering. Features in this list will be excluded from
HVG selection but remain in the output data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"MT-CO1"`, `"MT-CO2"`, `"MT-ND1"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_features_to_exclude`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
User-defined list of feature names to exclude from HVG calculation.
These features will be excluded from HVG selection but will remain in the output data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"MT-CO1"`, `"MT-CO2"`, `"MT-ND1"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

### QC metrics calculation options

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_qc_metrics`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys to select a boolean (containing only True or False) column from .var.
For each cell, calculate the proportion of total values for genes which are labeled 'True',
compared to the total sum of the values for all genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"filter_with_hvg"`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"ercc,highly_variable"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `","`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--top_n_vars`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of top vars to be used to calculate cumulative proportions.
If not specified, proportions are not calculated. `--top_n_vars 20,50` finds
cumulative proportion to the 20th and 50th most expressed vars.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `","`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--log1p_transform`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Compute log1p-transformed versions of the calculated QC metrics. For each emitted
metric column `<col>`, an additional column `log1p_<col>` is added containing
`log1p(<col>)`. Mirrors scanpy's `log1p` flag.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_obs_num_nonzero_vars`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of column in .obs describing, for each observation, the number of stored values
(including explicit zeroes). In other words, the name of the column that counts
for each row the number of columns that contain data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"num_nonzero_vars"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_obs_total_counts_vars`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the column for .obs describing, for each observation (row),
the sum of the stored values in the columns.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"total_counts"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_var_num_nonzero_obs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of column describing, for each feature, the number of stored values
(including explicit zeroes). In other words, the name of the column that counts
for each column the number of rows that contain data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"num_nonzero_obs"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_var_total_counts_obs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the column in .var describing, for each feature (column),
the sum of the stored values in the rows.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"total_counts"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_var_obs_mean`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the column in .obs providing the mean of the values in each row.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"obs_mean"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_var_pct_dropout`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the column in .obs providing for each feature the percentage of
observations the feature does not appear on (i.e. is missing). Same as `--num_nonzero_obs`
but percentage based.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"pct_dropout"`
:::
::::
:::::

### RNA Scaling options

Options for enabling scaling of the log-normalized data to unit variance and zero mean.
The scaled data will be output a different layer and representation with reduced dimensions
will be created and stored in addition to the non-scaled data.

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--enable_scaling`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Enable scaling for the RNA modality.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--scaling_output_layer`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Output layer where the scaled log-normalized data will be stored.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"scaled"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--scaling_max_value`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Clip (truncate) data to this value after scaling. If not specified, do not clip.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--scaling_zero_center`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If set, omit zero-centering variables, which allows to handle sparse input efficiently."
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_false`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/rna/rna_multisample/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/workflows/rna/rna_multisample);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/rna/rna_multisample/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
